title: Personalize-then-Store: Benchmarking and Learning Personalized Memory for Long-horizon Agents
abstract: arXiv:2605.25535v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Existing large language model (LLM) based memory systems apply universal, static policies that overlook a fundamental reality: the contexts that are worth storing in memory are different across users. This misalignment wastes limited memory budget on transient interactions while failing to preserve critical context for longhorizon tasks. To address this gap, we investigate an underexplored question: can LLM based memory systems learn personalized memory policies? We introduce PerMemBench, the first benchmark that jointly models multi domain interaction histories and cross user heterogeneity in agent use patterns to evaluate personalized memory systems. We further present the first empirical study of memory personalization, proposing session-level storage gating, a lightweight framework that selectively bypasses memory operations for transient sessions. translated_title: 先个性化后存储：面向长程智能体的个性化记忆基准测试与学习
translated_abstract: 现有的基于大语言模型（LLM）的记忆系统采用通用、静态的策略，忽视了一个基本事实：值得存储到记忆中的上下文因用户而异。这种错位导致有限的记忆预算被浪费在瞬态交互上，同时未能为长程任务保留关键上下文。为弥合这一差距，我们研究了一个尚待探索的问题：基于LLM的记忆系统能否学习个性化的记忆策略？我们提出了PerMemBench，这是首个联合建模多领域交互历史与跨用户智能体使用模式异质性的基准，用于评估个性化记忆系统。我们进一步开展了首个关于记忆个性化的实证研究，提出了会话级存储门控（session-level storage gating）——一种轻量级框架，可选择性地对瞬态会话绕过记忆操作。我们的研究证实，个性化策略能带来显著的记忆保留增益……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了首个个性化记忆基准PerMemBench，并设计了会话级存储门控这一轻量级框架，证明让LLM记忆系统学习因用户而异的个性化存储策略，可显著提升长程智能体任务中关键上下文的保留效果。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces PerMemBench, the first benchmark for evaluating personalized memory systems, and proposes session-level storage gating, a lightweight framework showing that learning user-specific memory policies yields substantial context retention gains for long-horizon agents.
